**Playbook — Sonar Picket (Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma role)**

**Hiding**
- With no feedback about opponents' aiming patterns, hiding is essentially a blind guess. Don't waste reasoning on it — avoid the most obvious cells (center 5, edges 1 and 9). Pick from {2,3,4,6,7,8}, varying round to round. Hiding at 7 twice in the later rounds while Gamma shot elsewhere worked acceptably; staying off center is fine.
- Track every shot fired at me across rounds and shift off cells I've been shot at in before. If a shooter repeats a cell against me, exploit that predictability by never being there.
- If a boat hits me in a cell, don't return to that cell or its neighbors.

**Firing**
- Follow the standing order (fire at the next live station around the picket). Don't waste shots off-target; hits pay 4 and nothing else pays except escort pairs.
- Vary my firing cell round to round rather than anchoring on one spot. In this episode varying (4, 6, 4...) produced two hits on Foxtrot — center-out cycling (5, then 4/6, then 3/7) plus tracking my own misses worked reasonably. Keep a mental list of cells I've missed at my current target and don't refire them unless several rounds have passed.
- Any information in notes about where a target is hiding — believe it only if that boat has been truthful before, but use it.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting, but Harbor's threat to put me off the board makes it strictly bad unless Harbor has demonstrably lost enforcement ability. Stay away. Nothing in this episode changed that.

**Claims**
- Always claim truthfully. The office validates against private truth and a false claim destroys credibility for zero gain. This held up all six rounds — keep it.

**Escort claims (highest value, but needs a real partner)**
- Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each per round — more than a hit (4). The theoretical dominant move is to negotiate a mutual escort with one other boat in notes and both name each other every round. That's still worth attempting in round 1.
- **What failed this episode:** I proposed a mutual escort deal in my round-1 note and repeated it later, but neither Foxtrot nor Gamma ever reciprocated. I then wasted escort claims ([salvage: Foxtrot] with no deal in place) that earned nothing — a unilateral escort claim pays zero unless the other boat names me back. Never file an escort claim for a boat that hasn't committed in notes or reciprocated before; claim [salvage: none] instead.
- Give the offer a hard deadline: propose in round 1, repeat once in round 2. If no boat has named me back or committed by end of round 2, drop the pitch and go quiet — the notes add nothing after that.
- If a boat does reciprocate once, lock it in and reconfirm in notes every round. If a partner reneges, drop them immediately and offer the deal to the other live boat.
- My +11 came from two hits plus truthful play; the escort channel was completely dead. So expect the shooting game to be the real game unless a partner shows up — don't sacrifice firing discipline chasing a deal that isn't happening.

**Notes**
- Round 1: propose the escort deal explicitly and briefly.
- Round 2: one repeat offer, then stop pitching if ignored.
- Later rounds: keep notes short ("steady on station" was fine) — or share truthful miss cells on my target to build trust, which might unlock an escort deal late. Don't spend effort on deception; the value is coordination.

**Priority order next time:** (1) offer the mutual escort deal once, hard deadline end of round 2, (2) if dead, default to [salvage: none] every round — never unilateral claims, (3) fire at the ordered target with varied, non-repeated cells, (4) claim truthfully, (5) never touch Harbor.

PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (as a firing boat, e.g. Foxtrot)

Hiding:
- Pick a uniformly random cell each round and never repeat or pattern my picks. Opponents who hit me did so by anticipating predictable choices (edges, repeats of previously safe cells). Randomize; do not "reason" toward a cell.
- Never hide adjacent to my own previous cell. In this episode I hid in cell 4 twice and got hit once — avoid reusing any cell I've already hidden in, even "randomly."

Firing:
- Fire at the standing-order target every round. It's the office-sanctioned channel and the only reliable point source (each hit is worth 4).
- Randomize the fire cell each round. Over 6 rounds of random cells at Gamma I hit twice — that's roughly what random fire yields, so keep expectations modest and keep firing even after misses.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal from the board, and losing remaining rounds costs more than 3 points. This held up — Harbor's threat kept everyone honest all episode.

Claiming:
- Always claim the true result of my shot. The claim must match the office's private info anyway; lying gains nothing and burns credibility.

Notes:
- Keep notes bland ("steady on station"). In this episode my elaborate escort-pact proposals in notes got zero uptake — everyone else just posted "steady on station" every round. Don't spend a note on negotiation again unless I see another boat actually using notes to talk.

Escort claims (still the big miss, strategy now revised):
- Mutual escort is worth 5 points each per round — up to 30 over the patrol — but it requires the other boat to name me back, and no boat ever did. Proposals via notes did not work; other boats either claimed none or claimed Harbor.
- New rule: name a live firing boat every round anyway (never "none", never Harbor). Naming none guarantees 0. Naming my shooter (the boat whose standing order targets me) each round is the best shot at learned reciprocity: they see my claim in the log, gain nothing from ignoring it, and gain 5 if they ever mirror me. Consistency is what teaches the pattern.
- In this episode I wasted rounds claiming "harbor" — Harbor doesn't file escort claims of its own, so a Harbor claim can never pair. Only name boats that are actually playing the claim stage.
- Do not fire on my intended escort partner if the standing order allows choice, so they have reason to reciprocate.

Scoring priorities, in order: mutual escort (largest, attempt every round by naming my shooter), standing-order hits second, never Harbor. Expect roughly one hit per 3 rounds of random fire; the escort channel is where the upside is, so work it every single round.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

When the escort stage is put to me, I name a boat every round, not "none." Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each, the single largest payoff in the game. I propose an escort partner publicly in my station note early ("Gamma escorts Foxtrot") and name that same boat each round. But I've now learned that a one-way announcement does not create reciprocity: I claimed Foxtrot all six rounds and never once got the mutual 5 points — I finished at +2 while partners who did pair up ran away with it. So the announcement alone isn't enough. If my named partner doesn't claim me back within a round or two, I switch my claim to the boat that IS claiming me (the escort history in the round summaries shows who claims whom), or to a boat I can bargain with via notes. Read the prior rounds' escort records before assuming my standing pairing is working.

When the claim stage is put to me, I report the office's private result exactly. The claim must match the true result; a false "hit" is an invalid move at best. This worked and stays.

When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order (fire at the next live station round the picket) and never fire on Harbor: 3 points isn't worth the explicit elimination threat. But my fire-cell selection needs a real change: I fired cell 5 at Echo in essentially every round and missed every time. Repeating the same cell against a target that keeps surviving is wasted — if my shot at a given cell misses, that cell is eliminated for that target until they've moved and shown a new pattern. Vary the cell each round, prefer cells the target hasn't been ruled out of, and track which of my cells have already missed. On a 9-cell line with random hiding most shots miss, but I maximized my miss rate by being maximally predictable.

When the hide stage is put to me, I randomize across cells rather than reasoning from "no one targets me" — I got hit twice by Foxtrot even while trying to be unpredictable, so this defense matters. Vary genuinely: no repeated cells, no gravitating to the mid. Avoid cells I just occupied or that an attacker has just fired at.

When the note stage is put to me, I use the note to coordinate: state my escort intent plainly and consistently — but make it a two-way ask, not a declaration ("Gamma claims Foxtrot for escort; Foxtrot, claim me back and we each clear 5 a round"). If the partner's notes or claims show no reciprocity by round 2 or 3, use the note to open a pairing with the other boat instead. A silent partner costs me nothing to keep claiming but earns nothing either.

What did not work: claiming [salvage: none] — fixed last time. This patrol's failure was different: I announced an escort pairing, kept it consistent for six rounds, and the mutuality never materialized. Consistency is only worth something if the other side answers; check the escort history each round and redirect to whoever is actually claiming me. Also, firing the same mid cell every round (5, five-plus misses, zero hits) — never repeat an already-missed cell against the same target.
